name: Chicken Alfredo Lasagna

ingredients.item: Frozen Lightly Breaded Chicken Breast Bites
ingredients.buy: 2 lb 5 oz, baked from frozen and roughly chopped
a generous pinch of each (about 1 1/2 tsp salt and 3/4 tsp black pepper)

writer_notes: Ledger reconciled both directions: all 8 locked ingredients are used by a step, and no step uses anything not on the buy list. No orphans, no invented ingredients.

The 'Salt' locked line folds black pepper into its buy string (about 1 1/2 tsp salt, 3/4 tsp black pepper). Both are consumed in the blend step (step 3), so pepper is not an orphan even though it lacks its own line.

FLAG: Source protein is 'Frozen Lightly Breaded Chicken Breast Bites' (breaded, pre-formed). Run condition names 'boneless skinless chicken breast.' Clears the band anyway (protein 40.7 >= 40, cal 496 in 450-800). Soft mismatch on protein form, not fixing.

Scale sanity: lines read as a consistent ~2.33x lift from the source recipe to 14 servings across every ingredient; no single line dominates or looks transposed.

The source used a 10.5x7.5 dish and suggested a 13x9 for a doubled batch; at 14 servings I wrote the method around the 13x9, consistent with the scaled quantities.

prose.intro_html: Lasagna usually lands on the naughty list for anyone counting macros, and I understand why. Most versions are a carb bomb wrapped in grease with a little meat waving from the window. This one flips the math. We blend low fat cottage cheese straight into the alfredo, so every single layer is carrying protein instead of just calories, and the breaded chicken does the heavy lifting on top of that. When the pan comes out, each of the 14 servings sits at 496 calories with 40.7 grams of protein. That is comfort food you can eat on a Tuesday and still look your goals square in the eye.
prose.shop_smart:
Here is how you fill the cart without overthinking it. You need 2 lb 5 oz of frozen lightly breaded chicken breast bites, so grab the bag size that gets you closest to that and let the freezer hold the rest for the next batch. Low fat cottage cheese is the quiet hero here, and you want 4 2/3 cups (2 lb 5 oz) of it. Do not chase fancy, plain low fat blends the smoothest and disappears into the sauce.

For the sauce itself, 1 3/4 cups of jarred alfredo does the job. The roasted garlic style the original recipe used is nice, but any jar on the shelf works, so buy the one that fits the budget. On cheese, you are after 1 lb 2 1/2 oz of fresh mozzarella, roughly shredded, and 2 1/3 cups of freshly grated parmesan (9 1/3 oz). Grating your own parmesan off a wedge melts and browns better than the shaker can, so buy a wedge if the store has one at a fair shelf price. Round it out with 21 no-boil lasagna sheets (about 12 3/4 oz) and a bunch of fresh parsley, since you only need 6 tbsp chopped. Season with a generous pinch of each, roughly 1 1/2 tsp salt and 3/4 tsp black pepper.
prose.make_it:
Preheat the oven to 425F. Bake or air fry the frozen breaded chicken bites according to the directions on the bag, then roughly chop them into bite size pieces once they are cooked. That is your protein staged and ready.

Now the trick that carries the whole dish. Blend the cottage cheese, the alfredo, and your salt and pepper together until it is smooth. You want no curds left, just a creamy sauce that reads like alfredo but is quietly loaded with protein.

Time to build. Coat the bottom of a 13x9 baking dish with a thin layer of that blended sauce, then lay down 3 lasagna sheets. Add another layer of sauce, then chicken, parsley, mozzarella, and parmesan. Repeat the stack until the dish is full, but only use parsley on the first two layers so the top does not scorch. Finish the very top with mozzarella and parmesan and nothing else.

Cover the dish and bake for 30 minutes. Uncover it and bake another 10 to 15 minutes, until the cheese is bubbly and browning around the edges. Garnish with a little fresh parsley and grated parmesan, then let it rest for at least 5 minutes before you slice. That rest is not optional if you want clean portions instead of a landslide.
prose.portion_html: This bakes as one pan, so we portion by weight, not by eyeballing squares. Once the lasagna has rested, set an empty container on your scale, zero it out, then weigh the whole cooked dish and divide that number by 14. Portion each container to that target weight and every meal carries the same 40.7 grams of protein and 496 calories, no favorites and no short-changed lunches. Cut squares if you like the look of it, but when the knife and the scale disagree, trust the scale.
prose.cost_closing_html: At {{cost_ps}} a serving, you are walking away with 14 real dinners, and each one brings 496 calories, 40.7 grams of protein, 34.4 grams of carbs, and 21.4 grams of fat. That is a full week of high protein comfort food for the price of a single restaurant plate of lasagna that would not come close to these numbers. This is what eating well on a budget actually looks like when you run it through the math.

head.description: A high protein chicken alfredo lasagna that meal preps into 14 servings at 496 calories and 40.7 grams of protein each. Cottage cheese blended into the alfredo does the work, and it fits any budget.
head.keywords: high protein lasagna, chicken alfredo lasagna, cottage cheese alfredo, meal prep lasagna, budget high protein dinner, 14 serving meal prep, high protein comfort food
steps: Bake or air fry the frozen breaded chicken breast bites according to the package directions, then roughly chop into bite size pieces.
Blend the cottage cheese, alfredo sauce, salt, and black pepper together until completely smooth.

Coat the bottom of a 13x9 baking dish with a thin layer of the blended sauce, add 3 lasagna sheets, then more sauce, chicken, parsley, mozzarella, and parmesan; repeat the layers, using parsley only on the first two, and finish the top with mozzarella and parmesan.
Cover and bake 30 minutes, then uncover and bake another 10 to 15 minutes until the cheese is bubbly and browning at the edges.
Garnish with fresh parsley and grated parmesan, rest at least 5 minutes, then portion across 14 containers by weight.
